name: Cloud skin

card.summary: A soft, matte-diffuse makeup look that blurs texture and pores so skin appears smooth and even.

quick.overview:
Cloud skin describes a makeup finish where skin looks soft, velvety and slightly blurred, rather than glossy. The look is built with complexion products that diffuse light.

The appearance payoff is even-looking skin with less visible texture and pores, usable in everyday makeup or photographs.
quick.how: People typically apply a primer, a light base or skin tint, and a setting powder or blurring product, often with a soft brush or sponge, to achieve a matte-diffuse finish.
quick.risks: Makeup can clog pores or irritate in some people; products with fragrance or heavy powders may bother sensitive skin.

lead: Cloud skin is a makeup look in which the complexion appears soft, velvety and blurred, with a hazy matte finish and a trace of natural glow. It is produced with makeup rather than treatments, and it aims to make pores and uneven texture less visible so skin reads as smooth and even in person and on camera. [1][2]

The term is credited to Dominic Skinner, a global senior artist at M.A.C Cosmetics, and was reported in Bustle in December 2022 as a shift away from both glassy, dewy skin and the heavy matte looks of earlier decades. [1] Entertainment Tonight covered it in February 2023 as a TikTok trend, describing it as essentially soft matte makeup that keeps some glow rather than the flat finish associated with matte makeup of the mid-2010s. [2]

chain: Prep skin and apply primer and a light base
Set with a blurring or powder product
angle.text: The finish scatters light so pores and uneven texture are less visible, giving a smooth, soft-focus look. It sits between glossy glass-skin looks and full matte.

paras: The look is defined by its diffused, velvety finish rather than a particular product. Bustle quotes it as a soft, hazy matte finish with a touch of natural glow, positioned between the glassy dewy look and the extreme matte of the 1990s. [1] Maybelline's guide describes it as balancing dewy glow with a velvety matte finish, giving a soft-focus, filter-like complexion that is less glossy than glass skin and less dry than full matte, and suitable for everyday wear. [3]

Published guides share a similar sequence. Skin is prepped with moisturizer and often a serum so it looks plump rather than shiny, followed by a pore-blurring or matte primer. [2][3] A matte, soft-matte or lightweight foundation or skin tint follows, concealer is placed only where needed, and powder is used sparingly, often only on oily areas such as the forehead, nose and chin. [1][2][3]

Blush and bronzer in matte or hazy formulas add dimension, and a setting spray or blotting paper can control shine. [2][3] Bustle's account recommends thin layers that are allowed to absorb, a brush with a tapered tip for a light, airbrushed application, and applying foundation only where coverage is needed. [1]
Brands named across these guides include Fenty Beauty, M.A.C, Maybelline, e.l.f., NYX and Laura Mercier. [1][2]

Maybelline's guide stresses oil control for oily skin through a matte primer, targeted powder and blotting paper. [3] It also advises a hydrating base using water-based or gel moisturizers. [3] Entertainment Tonight lists a moisturizer and serum prep step before primer in its routine. [2]

timeline.event: Bustle reports on cloud skin, crediting M.A.C Cosmetics artist Dominic Skinner with the term (article dated 7 December). [1]
Entertainment Tonight covers cloud skin as a TikTok beauty trend (14 February). [2]
